en: Record of the Meritorious Deeds Performed by the Śramaṇa Hóngmiào of Shazhou in the Great Tibetan Empire:
A Brief Account of Vaiśravaṇa and the Goddess of Fortune (*Śrī-devī*) Based on the *Ménshén Mǔ* and the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra*.
At that time, the World-Honored One was in the mountain to the left,
in the meditative concentration known as the First Watch of the Night.

Then the assembly of the Trāyastriṃśa devas and the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, having received their predictions, descended and offered various musical instruments, incense, and flowers to the World-Honored One.
When the offering was completed, the World-Honored One immediately bestowed a prediction upon the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, saying:
"In a future age, you shall attain Buddhahood;
your name shall be Nemirañca Vaiśravaṇa."
Having received the prophecy, he immediately made a great vow before the Buddha:
"Until I have attained Buddhahood, may I become a powerful Yakṣa King and protect this Jambudvīpa in the south."
All sentient beings in the world, including kings,
ministers, princes, and the people of the entire nation—
whether male or female— should respectfully pay homage and vow to faithfully accept the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa*.
May the fourfold assembly recite for me all the sūtras concerning past awakenings within that kingdom,
so that the people shall not suffer from famine or the spread of disease.
Neighboring states and hostile enemies will alternately inflict punishments upon one another;
violent rains and fierce winds will fail to subside;
and the seasons, the sun, and the moon will suffer eclipses.
A voice issued from within the well and the stars moved across the earth;
the people within the realm suffered various afflictions and distresses.
Thus, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of such calamities, portents, and evil events arose.
At that time, the World-Honored One said, "O King, Sovereign of Men, may you protect the kingdom.
You should always, within your realm, select a spacious and open location,
sprinkle the ground with fragrant water, and establish a single site for the Dharma assembly."
"Recite a single word for me. At that time,
as the Master was lecturing and reciting the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra*,
immeasurable hundreds of thousands of devas [were present].
Furthermore, the long-standing benevolent deities who protect the king,
as well as my own retinue, shall each conceal their forms to provide protection and assistance.
Now, those enemies will naturally submit.
Sorrow, illness, and pestilence shall likewise be eliminated;
all soldiers shall become entirely brave and robust;
and the people within the realm, having received [the king's] invitations, shall enjoy happiness.
The World-Honored One asked, "Is this true?
Then King Vaiśravaṇa replied.
The World-Honored One said:
"If there is a king who assists me by issuing such an invitation,
and I am not included among those present there, I shall not protect that king."
"I pray that you do not see me as a brother of a great kingdom;
I pray that you see me broken into seven pieces.
Having made this vow before the future Buddhas, he returned to his original celestial realm.
When the time arrived, the great assembly had gathered together.
Ānanda rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, joined his palms in reverence,
and addressed the Buddha, saying:
World-Honored One,
I am a worldling and do not understand the noble intention.
At the time of nightfall, celestial fragrant flowers were placed upon me.
The Śramaṇa Hóngbiàn of the Teaching School in Shazhou of the Great Fan [Kingdom] cultivated meritorious deeds.
The Imperial Scribe for the Characters of the Great Fan Kingdom, Xiànxí Jì,
was commanded by imperial decree to oversee the administration of Hexi.
